L149@P5-6: © Western Governors University October 27, 2026 6About Western Governors University
L150@P6: Why are we called Western Governors University? Our name tells the story of our founding—a story that dates back to
L151@P6: 1997, when a group of U.S. governors came up with an innovative answer to a question of growing concern: How can we
L152@P6: ensure more of our residents have greater access to a college education that fits their schedule? That meeting of the
L153@P6: Western Governors' Association marked the beginnings of a new national university.
L154@P6: From the beginning, we were designed to be different. The U.S. governors who founded WGU knew that the college
L155@P6: student of the 21st century would be very different from students in the past. For millions of working adults, the dream of
L156@P6: pursuing a college education could only become a reality once the boundaries of time and place could be removed.
L157@P6: Overcoming this challenge was at the heart of the WGU idea.
L158@P6: It was the mid-1990s, and a new technology was quickly emerging: the internet. As more and more Americans were able
L159@P6: to get online, the possibility of an ''anywhere, anytime'' education became a reality. And more than simply delivering
L160@P6: traditional, lecture-based learning via modem and monitor, our founders recognized that technology could be used to
L161@P6: fundamentally change the way college students learn. Harnessing the power of the internet and our innovative new
L162@P6: learning model—competency-based education—WGU revolutionized the way students learn, master concepts, and
L163@P6: progress to a degree.
L164@P6: As a nonprofit, online university founded by governors, WGU is different. But even beyond the unique story of our
L165@P6: founding and the foresight of our founders, WGU is different for a more fundamental reason: We do education differently.
L166@P6: WGU is mission-driven. Created to expand access to higher education through online, competency-based degree
L167@P6: programs, WGU’s mission has remained one of helping hardworking adults meet their educational goals and improve
L168@P6: their career opportunities. Our mission is to change lives for the better by creating pathways to opportunity.
L169@P6: WGU Core Academic Commitments support our mission to create pathways to opportunity by ensuring students receive
L170@P6: an education with value, integrity, relevancy, transparency, and personalization.
L171@P6: • Value: Advance the value of WGU's competency-based education model and credentials.
L172@P6: • Integrity: Base each credential on a relevant assessment of competence that is psychometrically sound and
L173@P6: assessed with integrity.
L174@P6: • Relevance: Align every competency to skills that can stack to high-value marketable skills, applicable knowledge,
L175@P6: and respected credentials.
L176@P6: • Transparency: Design skills, competencies, and credentials to be surfaced on a sharable learner-owned record.
L177@P6: • Personalization: Personalize pathways, pace, and support to ensure equitable access and attainment of
L178@P6: credentials.
L179@P6: WGU equips students with the skills employers want, backed by credentials employers trust.
L180@P6: Colleges and universities traditionally require attendance in a classroom, conferring degrees based on completion of a
L181@P6: certain set of courses for a given number of credit hours. As an online institution that provides its students the
L182@P6: convenience of studying and completing coursework outside the classroom, WGU provides competency-based courses
L183@P6: to complete its degree and non-degree requirements. Competency-based programs allow students to demonstrate that
L184@P6: they have acquired the competencies (levels of knowledge, skill, or ability) required for a particular degree or certificate.
L185@P6: Students have often acquired many of the skills necessary for a degree through life or work experience. WGU’s system
L186@P6: enables students to utilize previously learned skills in proving their competencies.
L187@P6: A team of faculty have identified the required competencies for each program offered at WGU. Competencies summarize
L188@P6: the critical knowledge and skill levels essential for mastery of a particular field. WGU students demonstrate mastery of
L189@P6: competencies by completing assessments. An assessment may be a test, a project, an essay, or another practical
L190@P6: demonstration of a required skill. Therefore, assessments might look like:
L191@P6: Core Academic Commitments
L192@P6: Competency-Based Education
L193@P6-7: © Western Governors University October 27, 2026 7• Assignments involving problem-solving in science or information technology.
L194@P7: • Computerized math examinations consisting of multiple-choice, matching, and other question types.
L195@P7: • Projects requiring the student to design a lesson plan about American history.
L196@P7: • Reflection essays about case studies.
L197@P7: • Research papers on particular topics within the student’s field.
L198@P7: Each assessment measures knowledge and skill in a given area through appropriate means. Assessments are
L199@P7: developed using a rigorous process that conforms to professional testing standards. This process yields high-quality
L200@P7: exams, reliable results, and supports valid conclusions about each student’s level of competence. Students can be
L201@P7: confident that all their assessments, whether computerized exams or performance tasks, align to and demonstrate
L202@P7: specific competencies in their individual degree programs.
L203@P7: Accreditation
L204@P7: Accreditation provides external, expert evaluation of WGU’s programs and policies, eases the transfer of credits to other
L205@P7: accredited institutions, and legitimizes degree credentials for employers and colleges.
L206@P7: NWCCU
L207@P7: Western Governors University is accredited by the Northwest Commission on Colleges and Universities. Accreditation of
L208@P7: an institution of higher education by the Northwest Commission on Colleges and Universities indicates that it meets or
L209@P7: exceeds criteria for the assessment of institutional quality evaluated through a peer review process. An accredited
L210@P7: college or university is one which has available the necessary resources to achieve its stated purposes through
L211@P7: appropriate educational programs, is substantially doing so, and gives reasonable evidence that it will continue to do so
L212@P7: in the foreseeable future. Institutional integrity is also addressed through accreditation. Accreditation by the Northwest
L213@P7: Commission on Colleges and Universities is not partial but applies to the institution as a whole. As such, it is not a
L214@P7: guarantee of every course or program offered, or the competence of individual graduates. Rather, it provides reasonable
L215@P7: assurance about the quality of opportunities available to students who attend the institution. Inquiries regarding an
L216@P7: institution’s accredited status by the Northwest Commission on Colleges and Universities should be directed to the
L217@P7: administrative staff of the institution. Individuals may also contact: Northwest Commission on Colleges and Universities;
L218@P7: 8060 165th Avenue NE, Suite 100; Redmond, WA 98052; (425) 558-4224; www.nwccu.org.

L346@P9: University Leadership Council
L347@P9: Academic programs are developed and guided by WGU administrators working through several councils comprised of
L348@P9: academicians and industry experts in the various fields of knowledge. Each programmatic area (e.g., undergraduate
L349@P9: nursing, initial licensure for teaching) has a program council which is the faculty governing body for the degree or nondegree program. Program councils, along with the program coordinator, are responsible for overseeing the development
L350@P9: of the curriculum (including competence descriptions, subdomains, and domains), overseeing all assessments, and
L351@P9: updating the curriculum.
L352@P9: In addition to program councils, an Assessment Council is responsible for working with program leaders, assessment
L353@P9: development vendors, and WGU assessment staff to ensure that WGU’s assessments are appropriate tests of the
L354@P9: competencies identified by the program leaders.
L355@P9: Faculty Composition
L356@P9: WGU employs a disaggregated faculty model across the university. The aggregated roles and tasks performed by
L357@P9: traditional university professors (e.g., meeting with and advising students, course or curriculum design, instruction,
L358@P9: assessment) are distributed among faculty members. Consequently, the jobs of individual WGU faculty members focus
L359@P9: on single aspects of the academic experience, and students are supported by a team of faculty. Within WGU, there are
L360@P9: several faculty roles and associated tasks:
L361@P9: Assessment Faculty – An individual with expertise in assessment theory and practice who is responsible for the design,
L362@P9: development, and continuous improvement of assessments that support a competency-based curriculum in accordance
L363@P9: with industry best practices.
L364@P9: Curriculum Faculty – An individual with expertise in curriculum theory and practice who is responsible for the design,
L365@P9: development, and evaluation of competency-based curricula to provide relevant, robust learning experiences.
L366@P9-10: © Western Governors University October 27, 2026 10Academic Calendar
L367@P10: The traditional academic calendar with limited enrollment periods, holidays, and other significant dates is not applicable.
L368@P10: In WGU’s continuous-enrollment model, new groups of degree-seeking students start on the first day of every month.
L369@P10: Students can access learning resources, schedule assessments, and complete performance assessments anytime.
L370@P10: WGU’s academic calendar divides a student’s academic year into two, six-month semesters called ''terms.'' The six
L371@P10: months that make up a term are based on when the student begins the program. For example, if a student begins the
L372@P10: program on February 1, the first term will last from February 1 through July 31. The second term would begin August 1.
L373@P10: Learning Resources
L374@P10: WGU students use a variety of learning resources, included in the cost of attendance, to acquire the skills and knowledge
L375@P10: needed to complete assessments. These learning resources come in a variety of forms (e.g., e-textbooks, web-based
L376@P10: tutorials, simulations, online labs).
L377@P10: Student Services
L378@P10: Students enrolling at WGU become part of our community of faculty and staff who are united under one goal: student
L379@P10: success. The Student Services office is available during extended hours to assist students with general questions and
L380@P10: administrative or accessibility issues. The Student Services team helps students resolve issues, listens to student issues
L381@P10: and concerns, and makes recommendations for improving policy and practice based on student feedback. The Student
